newsitem.title: BOSNIA: War looms in Bosnia unless action taken - report.
newsitem.headline: War looms in Bosnia unless action taken - report.

text.p: Bloodshed could return to Bosnia unless the international community acts decisively to bring indicted war criminals to justice and help refugees return to their homes, a watchdog agency has warned.

The International Crisis Group (ICG), a private monitoring commission with broad international membership, twinned its warning with a set of proposals to salvage the crisis-hit Dayton peace accord, which will be a year old on November 21.
The report was issued on Wednesday -- a day before foreign ministers gathered in Paris to discuss the international community's residual responsibilities in Bosnia.
While the U.S.-brokered Dayton peace agreement halted fighting it has not resolved the underlying causes of the 43- month conflict, the ICG report said.

"A window of opportunity remains half open, but unless the international community takes immediate and resolute action...(the peace agreement) may go down in history as an expensive ceasefire, not the basis for a lasting peace," the report said.

The report itemises Bosnia's outstanding problems, highlighting the fact that most of 75 indicted war criminals remain free and some still exercise power -- an issue ICG says "hangs like a sword of Damocles above the peace process".

The ICG also cited the September re-election of most of the same nationalist leaders who instigated the Bosnian war, problems in forming joint institutions and obstacles to repatriating 2.5 million refugees as threats to Dayton.

The International Crisis Group earned widespread respect when it helped unveil mass-scale manipulation in refugee voter- registration in August, prompting a postponement of Bosnia's municipal elections.
The organisation called upon the international community to "break the cycle of impunity" by tackling the issue of war crimes indictees head on.
Under the Dayton peace treaty, Bosnia's former factions are obliged to arrest and surrender all indictees to a U.N. war crimes tribunal.
Only seven indictees have been detained so far. The ICG said it was time for NATO-led peace forces to make the parties comply "by seeking out and arresting the indictees."
NATO repeatedly has said it will not stage manhunts for indictees and explains that it will apprehend them only if they are encountered in the normal course of NATO duties.

The recent lifting of the U.N.-imposed economic sanctions against Yugoslavia and the Bosnian Serbs was criticised by many as the squandering of a lever which could have been used to force compliance on the war crimes issue.

Billions of dollars in promised reconstruction aid for Bosnia was also seen as a source of potential leverage but the Serb side has made clear its willingness to do without aid rather than meet Dayton requirements to which they object.
